title: Nuclear–cell allometry
legend: Nuclear–cell allometry and allocation among selected large erythrocytes, using all 1,152 reviewed paired objects from 42 animals and 24 species. (a) Primary Pagel-lambda PGLS regresses log10 nucleus area on log10 cell area using released species medians, exactly reproducing the Figure 5 input summaries. The slope is unstandardized; slope one means proportional area scaling. The dashed slope-one reference passes through the log-scale species centroid. The solid line and gray ribbon show the fitted conditional mean and 95% t coefficient band; inference is conditional on fitted lambda. Point bars are released paired-object measurement intervals on both axes. The conditional regression does not correct predictor measurement error or establish a structural allometric exponent. (b) Open circles are animal medians of actual paired-object nucleus/cell fractions. Diamonds are species means of those animal medians, with equal animal weights. Species follow shared phylogenetic order; right-hand counts report animals / paired cells. Bars use 1,000 paired hierarchical resamples: sample animals within species, then paired cells within each sampled animal. Purple denotes the two direct developers; other species have aquatic larvae. (c) Conditional PGLS slopes and 95% t intervals compare released pooled medians with equal-animal means of animal medians, with and without D. aeneus and D. wrighti. The blue diamond and interval are the median and central95% range of 1,000 equal-animal bootstrap PGLS refits, re-estimating lambda; this is selected-measurement sensitivity, not a combined model confidence interval. Every model has species, not cells, as observational units. Seven species have one animal; their resampling intervals cannot represent among-animal uncertainty. One D. orestes animal contributes only one accepted cell, so within-animal dispersion is not estimable. Cells were selected for large area rather than randomly sampled from circulating erythrocytes; results describe that selected panel. Nuclear fraction and cytoplasmic area are derived paired quantities, not independent variables for causal path analysis. No cell, animal or species is removed from the primary analysis. Source-tree calibration/citation provenance remains unresolved. These exploratory complementary displays use unadjusted tests and do not establish physiological function or causal direction.
alt_text: Twenty-four labelled species show nucleus versus cell area on logarithmic axes, a conditional PGLS line and proportional-scaling reference.
